title: How to Compare Insurance Policies: The Apples-to-Apples Method
description: Learn how to compare insurance quotes and policies accurately: standardizing deductibles, matching liability limits, checking carrier ratings, and spotting hidden gaps.
author: Elena Rostova

content.text: Comparing insurance policies based solely on the monthly price is the single most common consumer mistake. A policy that costs $30 less per month often achieves that lower rate by stripping out vital liability coverage, raising deductibles to unaffordable levels, or inserting harsh exclusions.

rows: Set the exact same deductible ($500 or $1,000) on every quote.
A quote with a $2,000 deductible will falsely look cheaper than one with a $500 deductible.
Match bodily injury and property damage limits (e.g. 250/500/100).
Comparing state-minimum liability against high-limit coverage is not an honest comparison.
Ensure all quotes offer Replacement Cost, NOT Actual Cash Value.
Actual Cash Value deducts heavy depreciation on roofs, appliances, and personal belongings.
Verify an 'A' rating or higher from AM Best or Fitch.
A bankrupt insurer cannot pay your total loss claim during a regional catastrophe.

content.title: Check Customer Satisfaction Scores
content.text: Before switching carriers, check independent customer service rankings from [J.D. Power Insurance Studies](https://www.jdpower.com/business/insurance) and complaint ratio indices published by the [NAIC](https://content.naic.org/).

Visit our dedicated [Comparisons Center](/compare) to evaluate standard insurance debates, including [Term vs. Whole Life](/compare/term-vs-whole-life) and [HMO vs. PPO Health Networks](/compare/hmo-vs-ppo).

items.question: How often should I shop around for insurance quotes?
items.answer: Every 12 to 24 months. Carrier actuarial models update constantly, and switching carriers can often yield 15% to 25% savings if your profile matches a different underwriter's target tier.

content.text: Rate filings and discounts vary by regional carrier.
